body:
**Blocked by:** #1060, #1069
**Model tier:** low

## Context

Model tier rationale: This aligns one test-local helper with an existing production byte encoding and adds one focused fixture regression.

Both #1060 and #1069 edit this test file while changing credential scheme coverage. Apply the fixture correction after those overlapping edits; their titles and touch sets do not establish that they already include this normalization fix.

- PR #1117, finding `9e4a92169d`, `backend/packages/data/src/__tests__/externalCredentialsStore.test.ts:24`: The direct-seal fixture interpolates UUID text unchanged, while production credentialAssociatedData lowercases both identifiers.

## Task

Make the test-local `associatedData` helper lowercase both the tenant and item UUID before constructing `semprec:external-credential:v1:<tenant>:<item>` bytes. Keep the production helper private and unchanged. Add a focused integration case that passes uppercase UUID text containing letters to the direct-seal fixture and then reads the credential through the real store using the canonical identifiers in the proper tenant scope. Retain the lowercase round-trip and binding tests that survive the blockers; do not restore any retired master-only tests.

## Touches

- backend/packages/data/src/__tests__/externalCredentialsStore.test.ts (associatedData/insertTenantRow fixture and its normalization regression only)

## Scope

### In scope

Fixture associated-data normalization and its real-store decryption regression.

### Out of scope

Production encryption or credential-store behavior, scheme cutovers, migrations and unrelated fixture cleanup.

## Acceptance criteria

- For finding `9e4a92169d`, direct-seal fixtures given uppercase tenant and item UUID text produce the same associated-data bytes as lowercase input and decrypt through getDecryptedCredential under the canonical tenant/item identifiers; existing binding rejection tests remain effective.
